items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: I just did one three months ago with three baritones — Ronnie Cuber, Gary Smulyan and myself, and we did the music of Gerry Mulligan.

ctx.x: Well you’ve been able to get together with some of your contemporaries on the baritone on some of your records, right?

Oh, yeah. I recorded a duo, the first time I ever did it was with Pepper Adams and then we did one with three baritones, Cecil Payne and Ronnie Cuber. And I just did one three months ago with three baritones — Ronnie Cuber, Gary Smulyan and myself, and we did the music of Gerry Mulligan. And we took all Mulligan tunes. And maybe Gerry would roll over in his grave if he heard us playing it, but it was some interesting things. You know, with three different guys playing Mulligan’s music, of all the musics. But one…

items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: He has shared the stage and studio with Nick Brignola, Joe Lovano and Benny Green

ctx.x: Baritone saxophonist Gary Smulyan was born on April 4, 1956 in Bethpage, New York. His first big band work with Woody Herman was followed by stints with the Mel Lewis Orchestra, the Phillip Morris Superband and the Vanguard Jazz Orchestra. He has shared the stage and studio with Nick Brignola, Joe Lovano and Benny Green, and currently records as a leader on Criss Cross Records.
Gary was interviewed in Utica, New York on October 17, 2010 by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
